sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 14.7% a year from $96.6 billion in FY2017 to $331.8 billion in FY2026 [F1][F10][F221].
The shape is a steady climb with two step changes: revenue growth slowed to 6.9% in FY2023 [D311] before reaccelerating to 15.7% in FY2024 [D364] and 17.8% in FY2026 [D472].
The FY2024 step came from growth across each segment, with Gaming up 39% on the Activision Blizzard acquisition [P26][P33].
The FY2026 step was driven by Microsoft Cloud, with Intelligent Cloud revenue up on Azure and Server products and cloud services up 31% [P12][P17].
Microsoft Cloud contributed 16.2pp of the 17.8% revenue growth in FY2026 and reached 64.6% of revenue [D568][D472][D566].
Server products and cloud services added 11.0pp, driven by Azure and other cloud services, which grew 41% [D642][P12].
Microsoft 365 Commercial products and cloud services added 5.1pp on 16.2% growth, and Search advertising added 0.5pp [D649][D648][D775].
Operating income grew 20.8% against 17.8% revenue growth, an incremental margin of 53.3% [D473][D472][D498].
Operating costs grew 10.3pp slower than revenue, at 7.4% [D499][D491].
Operating margin reached 46.8% in FY2026, above the 41.7% window median and the 30.1% window low [F50][D975][D973].
Gross margin of 67.9% sat below the 68.2% window median, down 0.9pp as cost of revenue rose to 32.1% of revenue [F30][D981][D486][D449].
The gross-margin decline came from continued AI infrastructure investment and sales mix shift to Azure, offset in part by Azure efficiency gains [P11].
In FY2026 net margin of 40.3% sat 6.5pp below the 46.8% operating margin, lifted by $10.7 billion of other income [F70][F50][X124].
That other income included $6.5 billion of net gains on OpenAI investments, primarily the dilution gain from the OpenAI Recapitalization [P7].
Operating cash flow of $182.9 billion was 1.37x net income in FY2026, in line with the 1.34x of FY2025 [F100][D459][D405].
Free cash flow of $67.0 billion was only 0.50x net income, the window low against a 0.91x median, as capex reached 34.9% of revenue [F120][D460][D988][D990][D455].
Cash used in investing rose $66.9 billion, primarily on a $51.4 billion increase in additions to property and equipment [P1].
Capex of $115.9 billion ran at 3.38x D&A, up from 2.93x in FY2025 [F110][D461][D407].
Net cash was $72.9 billion, or 22.0% of revenue, against a -7.2% software peer median and the 83rd percentile of six peers [D465][D466][D1007][D1006].
Total debt fell to $40.3 billion while cash and investments held at $113.2 billion [D464][D463].
Buybacks of $22.3 billion plus dividends of $26.4 billion absorbed 72.7% of free cash flow [X147][X157][D468].
The diluted share count fell 0.2% to 7,453 million, so EPS growth of 31.6% slightly outpaced net income growth of 31.3% [D493][X137][D476][D474].
Free cash flow ran below 80% of net income in FY2025 and FY2026, at 0.70x and 0.50x [R1][D406][D460].
The gap is capex-led rather than earnings-led, so the risk is that AI infrastructure spending keeps free cash flow margin at its 20.2% window low [D982].
FY2017 pretax income, tax and receivables were later restated, and the pack uses the first-reported values [R2][R3][R4][X95][X105][X213].
This affects only the FY2017 base year, so the ten-year CAGRs carry a small data-quality caveat.
Capex as a share of revenue, at 34.9% in FY2026, falling back toward the 22.9% of FY2025 would confirm easing capital intensity in the FY2027 10-K [D455][D401].
Free cash flow margin, at the 20.2% window low, recovering toward the 30.3% window median would reverse the conversion trend in the FY2027 10-K [D982][D984].
Operating margin, at the 46.8% window high, holding above the 41.7% median would confirm the leverage trend in the FY2027 10-K [D974][D975].
